name: Light Orange-Yellow
lede: Light Orange-Yellow is a bright, warm yellow from Ridgway's 1912 atlas, filed by our library as a lighter child of Light Orange rather than a color with its own separate naming history.

sections.title: A bright child of Light Orange
sections.body:
Ridgway's 1912 atlas carries this tone on plate III, hue 17, notated 2.7Y 8.5/9.5 in the Munsell system [1]. The 1955 ISCC-NBS dictionary groups it under block 71, naming it moderate orange yellow, 4.0 units from Ridgway's reading [1].

Our library files it as a family variant under [[light-orange]], and its closest neighbors by measured distance are [[sunglow]], about 2.8 units away and more vivid, and [[dandelion]], almost the same color at 3.0 units [2]. [[mustard-yellow]] sits a little further, about 3.1 units off and duller [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body:
Our archive matches this tone in 123 of 23,781 paintings, about 0.52 percent, as photographed, more common than 60 percent of the named colors tracked [3]. It peaks in the 1400s, present in 1.0 percent of the 945 paintings from that century, 1.7 times its museums' expected rate [3].

Inside a painting it most often plays an accent, in 66 percent of its 111 clearly-ranked appearances, a rank computed within each canvas so varnish cannot fake it [3]. George Dawe carries it most, in 6 of his 50 works here, 6.5 times his museums' baseline rate, and it is also most over-represented in Indian paintings, 3.1 times the expected rate [3]. These are photographs of aged, varnished paintings, and the match is a computed color reading, not a pigment identification [3].

origin.named_after: a brighter modifier of the Light Orange family; undocumented beyond the naming system

openers: Light Orange-Yellow shows up as an accent color two times out of three, more than any other role.
